title: RuneScape Began as a Game That Broke at Ten Players
hook: In 1999 about 20 people tested a game called DeviousMUD, and its creator admitted it would break if more than 10 played at once. Two years later it became RuneScape. What year did you start playing?
script: Did you know RuneScape started as a game that could only handle about ten players? In July 1998, a young programmer named Andrew Gower began writing a text based game he called DeviousMUD. He soon added point and click controls and an isometric engine with hills, valleys and multi level buildings. He wrote all of it in Java so it could run inside a web browser. On March 28, 1999, he opened a public beta. About twenty people tested it. Andrew pulled the client within days, saying it was not really anywhere near finished. He admitted it would probably break if more than ten people tried to play at once. In October 1999 he started over with his brothers Paul and Ian. They worked under the name Jagex, which stood for Java Gaming Experts. The rewrite was renamed RuneScape in early 2000. On January 4, 2001, the beta went live from the Gower family home in Nottingham. That version is what players now call RuneScape Classic. Today Jagex says more than 300 million accounts have been created across the franchise. Not bad for a game that once feared its eleventh player. Follow for more gaming history.
